solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Drunk tattoo artist splitting parish priest’s mouth (6,4)

indicatorNotes.Drunk: a drunk tattoo is one reeling out of shape, so its letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.splitting: the new letters split P and P apart by sitting between them

blocks.note: PP, the letters written after a parish priest's name; they are pulled apart to hold the rest
RA = Royal Academician, the crossword's usual artist

annotation.surface: A tattooist, the worse for drink, comes between a parish priest and his mouth.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s reads as 'is': the wordplay is the mouth. The drunk artist is not one word; only 'tattoo' is shaken up, and RA follows it.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang term: old jocular British slang for the opening potatoes are shovelled into.

entries.clue: Rush job (6)

blocks.note: the verb sense: to hurtle along headlong, out of control
the noun sense: a line of work followed for life

annotation.surface: A rushed piece of work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rush job' reads as one phrase for hasty work; split it and each word is a separate sense of CAREER, one a verb, one a noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Two plain senses: the verb for hurtling along, and the noun for someone's working life.

entries.clue: American runs hotel in inferior novel (3,5)

indicatorNotes.in: the three letters go in the word for inferior

blocks.note: worse = inferior; it opens to take the other letters after its W
H = hotel in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: An American runs a hotel in a second-rate book.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inferior novel' reads as a put-down of one book; 'inferior' is the wordplay and 'novel' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Michael Morpurgo's book about a horse in the First World War, later a play and film.

entries.clue: Regularly send bit they’d prepared for publication (6)

indicatorNotes.Regularly: take letters at regular intervals, here every second one

blocks.note: the 2nd, 4th, 6th letters and so on: sEnD bItThEyD

annotation.surface: Someone is told to post off the part they have got ready for the press.
annotation.walkthrough: The even letters are the ones kept; the odd ones S, N, B, T, H, Y are thrown away.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word for text that has been corrected and shaped, ready to print.

entries.clue: Man on throne (4,4)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, one thing on another sits above it, so it comes first

blocks.note: the king is a chessman, the most important man on the board
throne is jokey slang for the lavatory, and so is the john

annotation.surface: A man sitting on a throne.
annotation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue is also a plain description of a monarch, and the lavatory sense of 'throne' is the joke.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: this English monarch of 1199 to 1216 sat on the throne.

entries.clue: Without drinks in boozer (4)

indicatorNotes.drinks: to drink something is to take it inside, so W/O takes IN in

blocks.note: w/o is the written short form of without

annotation.surface: Going dry inside a pub.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boozer' is British for a pub, which is the surface sense; here it is the person who boozes.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang, used straight: someone who hits the cheap wine hard is exactly one who boozes.

entries.clue: Turning rather old, I note details of my life? (7)

indicatorNotes.Turning: turning the string round makes it run the other way

annotation.surface: Someone getting on in years notes down the facts of their life.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turning rather old' reads as ageing, but 'turning' is the instruction applied to everything up to 'note'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the question mark admits 'my life' stands for anyone's summary of facts, as on a CV.

entries.clue: Significant work, essentially embracing completely the unknown? (3,4,6)

annotation.definition: Significant work, essentially embracing completely the unknown?

indicatorNotes.essentially: the essence of 'work' is its middle, OR
indicatorNotes.embracing: BIG...OR wraps round the next letters like arms

blocks.note: bang = completely, as in bang up to date

annotation.surface: A major work that tackles the whole of what is unknown.
annotation.walkthrough: BIG and OR embrace BANG THE, then Y ends it. Read as a whole, the clue also describes the theory itself.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: the cosmological theory is a major piece of work about the great unknown of how everything began.

entries.clue: Idolised one way or another (7)

indicatorNotes.one way or another: taken literally, the word reads the same whichever way you go

blocks.note: the same letters forwards and backwards

annotation.walkthrough: 'One way or another' sounds like a vague shrug, but it means literally: forwards or backwards, the word is the same.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: treating someone as a god is the extreme of idolising them.

entries.clue: Reduced number of bars in Leeds opening late surprised Dicky (13)

indicatorNotes.opening late: Leeds's opening letter is late, as in dead and gone, so L goes
indicatorNotes.Dicky: dicky means unsound or shaky, so the letters are shaken up

annotation.surface: In Leeds, a club opening late astonished a man called Dicky.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Late' means dead here, not delayed, and 'Dicky' looks like a name but means shaky. Leeds is a city in northern England.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic paraphrase: the bar is a unit of pressure, so fewer bars means lowered pressure.

entries.clue: Pepper with this wine’s beginning to verge on spicy (9)

annotation.surface: Kitchen advice: the start of a wine has a peppery edge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pepper' is the verb, to spray with shot, not the spice the surface suggests. 'Beginning' is not a first-letter signal: the fruit is where wine begins.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: small shot fired in clusters from a cannon, used to spray the enemy.

entries.clue: Come of age, wanting women’s company (5)

indicatorNotes.wanting: wanting in the sense of lacking, so the W goes

blocks.note: to come of age is to grow up

annotation.surface: Reaching adulthood, someone longs for female company.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wanting women's company' reads as desire; split it, and 'wanting women' removes W while 'company' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a company of actors or soldiers is a band of people together.

entries.clue: You are against a second liaison? (5)

indicatorNotes.against: against in the sense of leaning on, so the pieces sit side by side

blocks.note: a mo = a moment, a second

annotation.surface: Someone opposes a second affair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'You are' leads the clue but ends the answer: 'against' lets it lean on the other pieces from behind.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowed French word: an affair of the heart, often secret, which is what a liaison implies.

entries.clue: What helps broadcast short advert round state? (5,4)

indicatorNotes.short: shortened, so ADVERT loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.round: the shortened word is wrapped round the state like a ring, so it starts at R and runs on past the state

annotation.surface: Something that helps a brief commercial reach the whole state.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Short advert' tempts AD, the usual abbreviation, but that leaves too few letters; here the whole word loses only its tail and is laid in a loop.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: electromagnetic waves are what carry a broadcast signal to the listener.

entries.clue: It’s primarily used on chair and is blown up (3,7)

annotation.definition: It’s primarily used on chair and is blown up

indicatorNotes.primarily: first of all, so just the U of 'used'
indicatorNotes.blown up: blown apart, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A description of something you sit on that has to be inflated.
annotation.walkthrough: 'It’s primarily' reads as 'mainly', but 'primarily' reaches only 'used'; 'It’s' just opens the description.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: an inflatable pad is put on a seat and has to be blown up.

entries.clue: Abettor agreeing partially about means of execution (7)

indicatorNotes.partially: only part of the words is used

blocks.note: the letters sit across abETTOR AGreeing, and are then read backwards

annotation.surface: An accomplice half-agrees about how someone should be put to death.
annotation.walkthrough: This is a less common spelling of garrotte, with one R.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: a cord or iron collar used to strangle a condemned person.

entries.clue: Full as a result of eating nothing? (8)

indicatorNotes.eating: the word eats the O, so O goes inside it

blocks.note: through = because of, as in 'through no fault of his own'

annotation.surface: Feeling full having eaten nothing, which is the absurd picture.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a riddle about being full without eating; the answer takes 'full' in its other sense of complete.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of complete: a full inquiry leaves nothing out.

entries.clue: Use rent for refurbishing possessions provided by landlord? (7)

indicatorNotes.refurbishing: refurbishing is making over, so the letters are remade

annotation.surface: Tenants' rent goes on doing up the property the landlord owns.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole surface is about a rented property, which hides that the rent and use are only letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A legal sense: holdings of land or property on terms granted by the owner; the question mark covers calling them possessions.

entries.clue: Celebrated mathematician takes to teaching (8)

indicatorNotes.takes: the name takes TO inside it

blocks.note: Alan Turing, the codebreaker and computer pioneer

annotation.surface: A famous mathematician goes into teaching.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Takes to' looks like a phrase for starting a career; it splits into 'takes' as the instruction and 'to' as the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: giving lessons, often one to one.

entries.clue: Where one could keep flask in bag (3,6)

blocks.note: to bag is to pocket, take for oneself

annotation.surface: Somewhere to carry a flask, in a bag.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' is not a container signal here but a word for fashionable, and 'bag' is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the back trouser pocket that a hip flask is shaped to fit.

entries.clue: Drinks a lot of sake first (6)

indicatorNotes.a lot of: most of the letters, not all, are used

blocks.note: saKE FIRSt, all but the ends

annotation.surface: Downing plenty of sake before anything else.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sake' tempts a Japanese drink as the answer; it is only a place the letters hide.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: fermented milk drinks from the Caucasus are one kind of drink.

entries.clue: Muse ultimately make obscure covers more melancholy (5)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so only Muse's final letter is taken
indicatorNotes.covers: the word for obscure covers the E, holding it inside

blocks.note: to blur is to make obscure

annotation.surface: A poet's inspiration ends up clouded and gloomier.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Muse' looks like the definition or a poet's goddess; only its last letter is used.
annotation.definitionFit: A colloquial sense: blue means sad, and the comparative follows.

entries.clue: Concerted effort to import new pancake (6)

indicatorNotes.to import: to import is to bring in, so N goes inside

blocks.note: a blitz is an all-out concerted effort

annotation.surface: A joint push to bring in a new kind of pancake.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is a Yiddish word, so its spelling is less guessable than most.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a thin rolled pancake from Jewish cooking, usually filled with cheese.

entries.clue: Best available door, free from choice joiner (5)

indicatorNotes.free from: door is freed of the letters OR

blocks.note: out = available, as a new book is out
or is the word that joins alternatives

annotation.surface: An advert for the finest door on sale, no carpenter needed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Best' is the verb, to beat. 'Joiner' is a British word for a carpenter, but here it is a word that joins two choices.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: best is the verb here, to beat or surpass.

entries.clue: Was coach on the radio stressed? (4)

indicatorNotes.on the radio: on the radio things are heard, not seen, so go by sound

blocks.note: to coach is to teach, so 'was coach' is its past tense

annotation.surface: Was the coach tense during the broadcast?
annotation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the two words sound alike. 'Was coach' is odd English because it stands for a past tense.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the physical sense: stretched tight under tension; the question mark nods at the anxious sense.

entries.clue: Supplies item to facilitate tea making during school (9)

indicatorNotes.during: the urn comes during the other word, inside it

blocks.note: a tea urn boils water for tea

annotation.surface: Kitting out a school with equipment for making the tea.
annotation.walkthrough: The school is a school of fish, not a place of lessons.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to provide or equip with something.

entries.clue: Fresher greeting German outside university by noon (7)

indicatorNotes.outside: GER goes outside, round the university
indicatorNotes.by: by in the sense of beside, as in 'sit by me', so N follows U

annotation.surface: A first-year student greets a German at the university around midday.
annotation.walkthrough: YO and GER together go outside UN. 'Fresher' is British for a first-year student, which the surface uses; here it is simply 'more fresh'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: fresher in the sense of newer or less aged.

entries.clue: Service encountering this delays court action (3,4)

annotation.definition: Service encountering this delays court action

blocks.note: reads like a church or legal service meeting an obstacle; in tennis, a serve that clips something at the top of the net
sounds like a lawsuit held up; really play on a tennis court waits while the serve is retaken as a let

annotation.surface: Something that holds up legal proceedings when met by a service.
annotation.walkthrough: The court is a tennis court and the service a serve, not a legal one. A serve touching the cord at the top of the net is a let and must be taken again.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight in tennis: a serve that clips the top of the net is a let and must be retaken.
